chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan without an excuse, he said: 'He must free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people; and if he is unable, he should give charity according to his ability.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the hierarchical expiation (kaffarah) for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast, prioritizing freeing a slave, then fasting two consecutive months, and finally feeding sixty poor people. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on graduated financial and physical burdens, concluding with a flexible provision for those unable to afford the primary options, ensuring the obligation remains accessible to all socioeconomic classes.
